question.worked_solution:
This question requires the product rule. Let $u(x)=2{x}^{4}$ and $v(x)=(5x+3)^{2}.$ Then

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=8{x}^{3},\,{v}^{′}(x)=10(5x+3).
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $v.$

Now, applying the product rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x) \\  & =(8{x}^{3})(5x+3)^{2}+(2{x}^{4})(10(5x+3)) \\  & =8{x}^{3}(5x+3)^{2}+20{x}^{4}(5x+3) \\  & =[8(5x+3)+20x]{x}^{3}(5x+3) \\  & =[60x+24]{x}^{3}(5x+3) \\  & =12{x}^{3}(5x+2)(5x+3).\end{aligned}
$$
